partyReviewGaps.title: Guest-seat dash / vault / hop movement is never predicted: rubber-banding and a G5b.2 regression
partyReviewGaps.why: The new skills move the caster, but only on the host: Shoulder Charge 2.4 u, Fox Step 2.0 u, Vault Shot 1.6 u, and the Pursuit 1.2 u and Disengage 1.0-1.8 u nodes. src/net/reconcile.js predicts a guest's own walk and dodge only. Any error above CORRECTION_SNAP_U = 1.0 u snaps instead of smoothing. So every one of these casts on a human guest seat shows a round-trip lag followed by a snap, which breaks the certified G5b.2 bars (predErr p95 <= 0.15 u at N1, max <= 1.0 u at N2/N3, no correction > 0.1 u per frame). PLAN §16.3/§16.5 only extend the action shadow's cooldowns, and reconcile.js is not in PARTY's edit list. It is also undefined what a dash does on an AIMED human cast: fireHumanSkill uses an aim direction with target: null, but §25.2 says 'toward the target'. GP.4 checks events, VFX and audio but never the guest's position error. Needed: define aim-based dash/vault/hop direction and distance for human seats, predict it in reconcile.js the way the dodge is predicted (or give an explicit bounded-correction policy), and add a GP.4/GP.9 check of predErr/snaps during these casts.

partyReviewGaps.title: Deadlines are only armed when a page opens, so a drop-in can stall the party page forever
partyReviewGaps.why: §16.3 sets deadlines 'only when humans >= 2', read when the page, door or shop opens. §25.7 says ownership follows seat control live. Failure case: the host is the only human and uses Manual mode, so AI-held cards open undecided and no deadline is set. A guest drops in onto one of those seats. That card is now human-owned and undecided, the host cannot decide it (not_owner), and nothing ever times it out. That is exactly the 'silent picker' the user ruled out. Also unspecified: (a) what happens to undecided AI-held Manual cards at a deadline (§16.3 only autopicks undecided HUMAN cards); (b) a network save carries run.party.deadlineTick, so loaded as single-player it would time out a solo player, contradicting 'single-player never shows a countdown'. Fix: arm or re-arm page/door/shop deadlines whenever humans becomes >= 2 while a decision is open, give a newly human-owned undecided card a fresh 30 s, apply the AI suggestion to every undecided card at a deadline, clear deadlines on a single-player load, and add these cases to GP.9.

partyReviewGaps.title: Shop in Suggested mode: opening an AI-held tab cancels that character's buys
partyReviewGaps.why: §25.6 says an AI-held tab 'the player never opened during this visit buys the AI's picks on Advance', and §16.3 applies AI buys only for untouched seats. Viewing a tab is therefore a commit, which contradicts the same section's rule 'Switching is navigation, never a commit'. It also differs from the party page, where an AI card stays pre-decided when viewed. A player cannot preview what the AI would buy for the Tank without cancelling it. The natural 'look at each character's shelf, then Advance' loses up to 3 nodes per ally per level, and the unspent Glint is worthless after the Level 3 shop. GP.7 cannot see this because the autopilot never opens tabs. Fix: show the suggested buys pre-marked on each AI-held tab (visible, toggleable), apply them on Advance unless the player un-marks them or buys on that tab, and add a GP.12 real-input check (view every tab, Advance, suggested buys still happen).

partyReviewGaps.title: The performance and bandwidth stress gates cannot produce the 'four full builds' they name
partyReviewGaps.why: GP.15 and GP.10 require 'four full builds' via ?level=3&partygrant=3. The proposed STARTER_GRANT[3].allies is 24 nodes + 2 legendaries = 26/32 per ally, and it is still subject to re-measurement. Whether ?partygrant stacks with the ally grant a Level-3 start already applies is unspecified. The composition is also random auto-fill, so the worst case is never measured: three allies stacking instance multipliers (Echo recasts, Multiply, Split, Bounce, Skewer, Scatter's 3 zones or shards, Detonate, Resonance) on top of the Healer's build. That stack is exactly what drives events/s, frame spikes and downstream KB/s. Fix: define a deterministic max-stress build per class (32/32 with the instance-multiplying nodes, e.g. ?partygrant=max or a partyStress cmd), make it the precondition for GP.10 and GP.15, and state whether ?partygrant stacks with a level start's grant.
